data.question_intent: Inquiring about the bank's ability to meet its cost target in light of potential macroeconomic shifts.
data.question_quote: So, you realised £200 million of the expected £500 million, for FY25. Do you see any execution risks for the remaining £300 million? And I know we've touched upon macro today and even last week, but just say there's a shift in the macro in the second half. Are you confident that you'll be able to see that remaining £300 million.
data.answer_quote: Okay, so just a reminder everybody, we got £2 billion target for the three years together. Actually, at the end of the first half of the plan we're at £1.35 billion. So, we've done £350 million of the £500 million that we need to do this year at the half year. So, £1.35 billion through that £2 billion and we've got a good line of sight here in relation to the execution of that.
data.reason: The answer directly addresses the bank's progress towards the cost target, acknowledges the impact of inflation, and discusses the bank's focus on efficiency and technology to mitigate risks, aligning with the question's topics.
